subject: geography
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which is a PRIMARY effect of a tropical storm?
options: Disease spreading from contaminated water afterwards
Buildings destroyed directly by strong winds
Loss of tourism income months later
questions.explain: Wind damage to buildings happens directly during the storm, making it a primary effect.

questions.q: A tsunami can be triggered when an earthquake occurs:
options: Under the sea, displacing a large volume of water
At the centre of a plate only
questions.explain: An undersea earthquake suddenly displaces water, generating tsunami waves.

questions.q: At a constructive (divergent) plate margin, the plates are:
questions.explain: At constructive margins plates move apart and new crust forms from rising magma.

questions.q: Which scale measures earthquake magnitude on a logarithmic scale, so each step is ten times greater in amplitude?
questions.explain: The Richter scale is logarithmic, so each whole number is a tenfold increase in measured amplitude.

questions.q: When two continental plates collide at a collision margin, the result is usually:
questions.explain: Neither continental plate subducts easily, so sediment and crust crumple upward into fold mountains.

questions.q: The point inside the Earth where an earthquake originates is called the:
questions.explain: The focus (or hypocentre) is the underground point where the earthquake starts.

questions.q: Which is a method of earthquake PROTECTION rather than prediction?
questions.explain: Earthquake-resistant building design protects people, whereas monitoring is prediction.

questions.q: Composite (stratovolcano) volcanoes are typically found at which margin?
questions.explain: Composite volcanoes with violent eruptions form at destructive margins where subduction melts crust.

questions.q: In which atmospheric cell does cold air sink at the poles, creating high pressure?
questions.explain: In the Polar cell, very cold dense air sinks at the poles forming high pressure.

questions.q: The most intense winds and heaviest rain in a tropical storm occur in the:
questions.explain: The eyewall, the ring of towering clouds around the eye, has the strongest winds and rain.

questions.q: Why do earthquakes occur at conservative plate margins?
options: Plates lock together then suddenly jolt as built-up pressure releases
One plate melts into the mantle
New crust is created very quickly
questions.explain: Friction locks the sliding plates until stored pressure is released suddenly as an earthquake.

questions.q: Convection currents that move tectonic plates occur in which layer?
questions.explain: Heat-driven convection currents in the semi-molten mantle drag the plates above.

questions.q: A conservative (transform) plate margin is one where plates:
questions.explain: At conservative margins plates slide past each other, so crust is neither created nor destroyed.

questions.q: Shield volcanoes, which produce runny lava and gentle eruptions, are mostly found at:
questions.explain: At constructive margins, basaltic lava is runny and forms broad, gently sloping shield volcanoes.

questions.q: The calm, clear centre of a tropical storm is called the:
questions.explain: The eye is the calm low-pressure centre, surrounded by the violent eyewall.

questions.q: Earthquakes can cause liquefaction, which is when:
options: Saturated soil behaves like a liquid and buildings sink
questions.explain: Shaking makes water-saturated soil lose strength and act like a liquid, so structures sink or topple.

questions.q: Volcanoes and earthquakes are mostly found:
options: In the centre of tectonic plates
questions.explain: Tectonic hazards concentrate at plate boundaries where plates interact.

questions.q: Which is a LONG-TERM response to a tectonic disaster?
questions.explain: Rebuilding to better standards takes months or years and is a long-term response.

questions.q: Which of these is a SECONDARY effect of an earthquake?
options: Fires caused by ruptured gas pipes
questions.explain: Fires from broken gas lines occur after the shaking, making them a secondary effect.

questions.q: Which is an example of an IMMEDIATE (short-term) response to a tectonic disaster?
questions.explain: Search and rescue happens in the hours and days straight after the event.

questions.q: Which is the strongest piece of EVIDENCE for recent climate change?
options: Rising global average temperatures and shrinking ice sheets
questions.explain: Records of rising temperatures, melting ice and sea-level rise evidence climate change.

questions.q: Why do many people continue to live in tectonically active areas?
options: Fertile volcanic soils and geothermal energy
There is no other land available anywhere
questions.explain: Volcanic areas offer fertile soils, geothermal energy, tourism and mineral resources.
